summary: Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (1829–1870) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and also taught the latter.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon, where he held an honorary associate post attested in 2019.

Chris Williams works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he studied at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer while serving on the teaching staff as an MPhil and PhD student.

Christian August Brandis (1790–1867) studied at Kiel University (~1808–1812), working in philosophy and history/archaeology. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1815–1821), and University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae (1855–1925) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology, having studied under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1879–1885), Münster (~1885–1898), Giessen (~1898–1901), and Heidelberg (~1909–1924).

Christian Bernert works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed a Magister der Philosophie under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Karin Preisendanz, Gerald Hödl, and Junjie Chu.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen (under Heyne), Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as Prussian envoy (~1841–1854).

Christian Coseru studied at the University of Bucharest and Australian National University. A specialist in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held posts at the College of Charleston (~2006) and UC Berkeley (~2018), alongside research affiliations in India.

Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who earned a master's degree from Leipzig (1748–1752). He served at the University of Göttingen as professor from 1763 and as library director (1764–1812).

Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, among others, holding a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA and PhD at Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Antioch, Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel, working in Indology and linguistics. He served as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876) at Bonn.

Christian Lee Novetzke is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia (PhD 1996–2003). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and the University of Washington (2007).

Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate by 1982 at the University of Copenhagen, where he also served as professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits earned his Magister and PhD at the University of Vienna. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he held posts at Vienna, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2012).
Christian Matthias Boehm specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) and studied under Toshifumi Konno.

Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2011) and Kyoto University, including as professor (attested 1993, 2008).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1883–1888). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and as a professor at Leiden (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and served as professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).
